lessons.title: The Prophet of Nineveh
lessons.body:
Yunus (AS) was sent to the city of Nineveh — a great metropolis in the region of Mosul, in modern-day Iraq. Some narrations say it held over a hundred thousand people, perhaps more. Others say it was larger still. It was one of the great cities of the ancient world.

The people of Nineveh were idolaters. They worshipped statues, carved gods, and the sun and moon. They had no scripture, no prophet before Yunus, and no memory of tawhid. They had inherited their religion from their ancestors — and their ancestors had been wrong.

Yunus called them to Allah. He warned them of the punishment. He called them to abandon their idols. And they refused. Day after day, week after week — nothing. They mocked him. They dismissed him. They continued in their shirk.

Yunus had delivered the message. He had warned them again and again. And when they still refused, he made a decision that would change the course of his life: he left. Not because Allah commanded him to — but because he was frustrated. He had had enough.

This is the beginning of the story of Yunus — the only prophet in the Quran whose story is named after him, and one of the most beloved stories in all of Islam.

dialogue.arabic: وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ ۝ إِذْ أَبَقَ إِلَى الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ
dialogue.translation: And indeed, Yunus was among the messengers. When he ran away to the laden ship.

lessons.didYouKnow: Nineveh is one of the oldest cities in the world — its ruins are near modern Mosul in Iraq. The Quran calls Yunus's departure abq, a word used for a slave running away from his master. It was not a dignified exit — it was a flight.
lessons.takeaway: Even a prophet can become frustrated — but frustration is not permission to abandon the mission.

lessons.title: The Departure
lessons.body:
Yunus left Nineveh. He did not ask Allah for permission. He did not wait for a command. He simply walked out — angry at his people, angry at their stubbornness, and perhaps angry at his own inability to change them.

The Quran uses the word abq — fleeing like a runaway slave. Yunus fled from his mission. He fled from his people. He fled from the responsibility that Allah had given him. And he thought that he could escape — that by leaving Nineveh, he could leave behind the burden of prophethood.

He walked until he reached the sea. There, a ship was preparing to depart. He boarded it — without asking where it was going, without caring where it would take him. He just wanted to be somewhere else. Anywhere but Nineveh.

But the Quran says something quietly ominous: And indeed, Yunus was among the messengers. He was still a prophet. He was still sent by Allah. And no matter how far he ran, he could not run from his Lord. Because his Lord was with him on the ship, in the sea, and in the belly of the whale — everywhere he went.

This is the first lesson of Yunus's story: you cannot escape the mission of Allah. You can leave a place. You can leave a people. You can leave a responsibility. But you cannot leave Allah. He is wherever you are — and His plan for you follows you wherever you go.

dialogue.arabic: وَذَا النُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَاضِبًا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ
dialogue.translation: And Dhun-Nun, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree anything upon him.

lessons.didYouKnow: The title Dhun-Nun means 'the companion of the fish' — one of the names given to Yunus in the Quran. Another title is Ṣāḥib al-Ḥūt — 'the companion of the whale.' Both refer to the most famous moment of his life.
lessons.takeaway: You cannot run from Allah — you can only run deeper into His plan.

lessons.title: The Casting of Lots
lessons.body:
The ship sailed. And then, as often happens at sea, a storm arose. The waves grew. The ship was overloaded. The captain realised they had to lighten the load — someone had to be thrown overboard.

The Quran says: And the ship was heavily laden. And he drew lots and was among the losers. They drew lots, and the lot fell on Yunus. Three times the Quran refers to this moment — and each time, the lot fell on Yunus. He was chosen to be thrown.

Look at the moment. Yunus had fled Nineveh to escape his mission. He had boarded a ship to escape his responsibility. And now, the sea itself demanded him. The waves rose, the ship groaned, and the lot fell — again and again — on the very man who had tried to run.

Some scholars say the sailors were reluctant to throw him. They had seen his dignity, his character. They cast lots a second time, then a third — and each time, the lot fell on Yunus. Finally, Yunus himself told them: I am the one. Throw me overboard. He did not argue. He did not beg. He accepted the decree of Allah — even the decree that meant drowning.

He was thrown into the sea. And the sea was not done with him yet. Because waiting beneath the waves was something prepared for him from before he was born — a whale.

dialogue.arabic: فَسَاهَمَ فَكَانَ مِنَ الْمُدْحَضِينَ ۝ فَالْتَقَمَهُ الْحُوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ
dialogue.translation: And he drew lots and was among the losers. Then the whale swallowed him, and he was to blame.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Arabic word al-mudḥaḍīn — 'the losers' — is used specifically for those who lose in a draw. The image is vivid: Yunus drew lots three times, and each time, he lost. And it was not really a loss — it was the beginning of his rescue.
lessons.takeaway: What looks like losing the draw may actually be the hand of Allah choosing you for something you cannot yet imagine.

lessons.title: The Belly of the Whale
lessons.body:
The whale swallowed Yunus. The Quran says: Then the whale swallowed him, and he was to blame. Blameworthy — because he had left his mission without permission. He had fled from the task Allah had given him. And now he was in the belly of a whale, in the darkness of the sea, in a place no human being had ever been before.

Think about what Yunus saw. No light. No sound except the ocean around him. No hope of escape. He was in the belly of a creature of the deep, deep under the water, with nothing but his own thoughts and his own duas.

The classical scholars describe the layers of darkness surrounding Yunus. The darkness of the whale's belly. The darkness of the ocean. The darkness of the night. Three layers of blackness — no light from any direction. Total, absolute, hopeless darkness.

And then — in that place where no one could hear him, no one could help him, no one could even know where he was — Yunus made a dua. And that dua would be preserved in the Quran forever. It would become the dua of every desperate believer, in every generation, in every kind of darkness.

dialogue.arabic: فَالْتَقَمَهُ الْحُوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ
dialogue.translation: Then the whale swallowed him, and he was to blame.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ said: Do not ask me about the whale that swallowed Yunus — it was a whale of the sea, and it swallowed him in the darkness of the deep. The story is preserved in revelation exactly because it teaches something the Prophet ﷺ wanted every Muslim to remember.
lessons.takeaway: Sometimes Allah has to take you to the darkest place you have ever been before you can see the light.

lessons.title: The Dua of the Whale
lessons.body:
In the belly of the whale, in three layers of darkness, Yunus made a dua. And it is one of the shortest duas in the Quran — and one of the most powerful:

La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin.

There is no deity except You. Exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.

Three sentences. A testimony of tawhid. A declaration of Allah's perfection. And an admission of his own fault. Yunus did not blame his people. He did not blame the whale. He did not blame the sea or the storm or the sailors. He blamed himself. Inni kuntu minaz-zalimin — I have wronged myself.

The Prophet ﷺ said that no one who calls upon Allah with this dua will be left unanswered — because it contains everything a servant needs to say. It affirms the Oneness of Allah. It glorifies Him. It humbles the one who says it. It accepts responsibility. It does not shift blame. It does not justify. It simply says: My Lord, I have wronged myself — and there is no god but You.

In the darkest possible place, in the most hopeless possible moment, Yunus found the exact words that every soul needs to say to its Lord. And Allah heard him.

dialogue.arabic: فَنَادَىٰ فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ أَن لَّا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
dialogue.translation: So he called out in the darknesses: There is no deity except You. Exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.

lessons.didYouKnow: This dua — La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin — is called Duʿāʾ Yunus and is one of the most beloved duas in Islamic tradition. The Prophet ﷺ said that no Muslim says it in supplication for anything except that Allah answers him.
lessons.takeaway: The best dua in your darkest moment is the one that glorifies Allah and admits your own fault.

lessons.title: The Command to the Whale
lessons.body:
The dua was answered. The Quran says: So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.

Notice the order. Yunus called. Allah answered. The whale — an enormous creature with no reason to spit out its food — obeyed the command of its Lord and released him. The sea, which had accepted the whale's swallow, gave Yunus back to the shore. And Yunus emerged onto dry land — exhausted, naked, and completely raw.

The Quran says: Then We cast him onto the bare shore while he was ill. He was sick. His skin had been affected by the acids of the whale's stomach. His body was weak. He was a man reduced to nothing — no mission, no people, no dignity, no strength.

And then Allah did something tender: And We caused a gourd vine to grow over him. A plant grew to give him shade. Its broad leaves covered his naked body. Its fruit gave him food. In the middle of a barren shore, Allah provided shelter for the prophet He had just saved.

This is the mercy of Allah for His servants. He does not just save you from the whale — He gives you shade on the shore. He does not just answer your dua — He provides for you after the answer. Every step of Yunus's recovery was a gift from his Lord.

dialogue.arabic: فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُنجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
dialogue.translation: So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.

lessons.didYouKnow: The classical scholars say the gourd plant that Allah grew for Yunus was a yaqṭīn — a broad-leafed plant whose leaves give shade without attracting insects. It was the perfect provision for a prophet who had lost everything.
lessons.takeaway: Allah does not just save you — He provides for you after He saves you.

lessons.title: The Plant and the Prophet
lessons.body:
When Yunus recovered, the Quran says: And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more. And they believed, so We gave them enjoyment for a time.

Wait — is this the same Nineveh? Yes. When Yunus left Nineveh, he did not know it — but his departure had shaken the people. They had seen a prophet leave them. Some narrations say they had seen the signs of punishment beginning to appear in the sky. And they had realised — too late, they thought — that Yunus had been telling the truth.

The entire city repented. Every man, woman, and child. They turned to Allah. They abandoned their idols. They cried out for forgiveness. And Allah — the Most Merciful — accepted them. The punishment was lifted. The city that had mocked its prophet for years became a city of believers overnight.

Yunus — who had fled Nineveh because he thought his people would never believe — returned to a city that had already believed. He had given up on them, but Allah had not. He had fled the mission, but Allah had finished it in his absence. His fear that his people would never turn was proven wrong by the very people he had abandoned.

This is the lesson. The change of hearts is not in our hands. We call. We warn. We invite. And then Allah — who owns every heart — does the work. Sometimes He does it in front of us. Sometimes He does it after we have left. But He never stops.

dialogue.arabic: فَآمَنُوا فَمَتَّعْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
dialogue.translation: And they believed, so We gave them enjoyment for a time.

lessons.didYouKnow: The people of Nineveh are the only nation in the Quran who were spared after the punishment had already been decreed. Allah says: Then why was there not a city that believed and benefited from its faith except the people of Yunus? (Yunus 10:98) Their repentance is unique in revelation.
lessons.takeaway: The change of hearts is not in our hands — Allah can turn a nation overnight, whether we are there or not.

lessons.title: The Only Reprieved Nation
lessons.body:
Among all the nations mentioned in the Quran — the people of Nuh, the 'Ad, the Thamud, the people of Lut, the people of Shuayb, the people of Musa and Fir'awn — only one nation ever avoided the punishment after it had been decreed. And it was the people of Yunus.

The Quran says: Then why was there not a city that believed and benefited from its faith except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in worldly life and gave them enjoyment for a time.

Look carefully at what this means. The other nations — every one of them — were given warnings. They were given messengers. They were given years to respond. And they refused. So the punishment came. But Nineveh was different. When Nineveh finally believed — after Yunus had already left, after the punishment was already at their door — Allah relented. He lifted it. He forgave them.

This is the mercy of Allah. Even when the punishment has been decreed, even when the prophet has already walked away, even when the city has been marked for destruction — the door of tawbah remains open until the very last moment. The people of Nineveh proved that no one is beyond forgiveness — as long as they are still alive to ask for it.

dialogue.arabic: فَلَوْلَا كَانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ فَنَفَعَهَا إِيمَانُهَا إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّا آمَنُوا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمْ عَذَابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا
dialogue.translation: Then why was there not a city that believed and benefited from its faith except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in worldly life.

lessons.didYouKnow: The repentance of Nineveh is celebrated in Surah Yunus (chapter 10), which is named after the prophet. It is the only surah named after a prophet whose entire story is about a nation's repentance.
lessons.takeaway: The door of tawbah is open until the very last moment — never assume anyone is beyond forgiveness.

lessons.title: The Lesson of Patience
lessons.body:
The Quran does not condemn Yunus for leaving Nineveh. It records it — but it treats it as a moment of human weakness, not as a sin. And then it gives us the lesson: So be patient, O Muhammad, as were the messengers of strong will, and do not be like the companion of the whale.

This is the Quran's lesson from Yunus's life. The Prophet ﷺ was told: Do not be like the companion of the whale. Do not leave your people in frustration. Do not give up on them because they did not respond. Do not assume that because your message is not working, the mission is over.

Yunus's impatience was real. His frustration was understandable. But it was not the way of the prophets of strong will — Ibrahim, Nuh, Musa, and Muhammad ﷺ. They did not leave. They did not give up. They did not flee. They stayed with their people for decades, through mockery and rejection, through every frustration — because they knew that the harvest belonged to Allah, not to them.

The Prophet ﷺ himself lived this. When he was driven out of Ta'if — stoned, bleeding, mocked — he did not curse the city. He said: Perhaps Allah will bring from their descendants those who will worship Him alone. Yunus fled in frustration; the Prophet ﷺ stayed in hope. This is the difference between the companion of the whale and the Prophet of mercy.

dialogue.arabic: فَاصْبِرْ كَمَا صَبَرَ أُولُو الْعَزْمِ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ الْحُوتِ
dialogue.translation: So be patient, as were the messengers of strong will, and do not be like the companion of the whale.

lessons.didYouKnow: The ulū al-ʿazm — messengers of strong will — are generally considered to be Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad ﷺ. These are the prophets whose patience was the most extraordinary, and whose missions lasted the longest.
lessons.takeaway: The mission of a believer is patience — not because success is guaranteed, but because the outcome belongs to Allah.

lessons.title: The Prophet of the Fish
lessons.body:
Yunus is called Ṣāḥib al-Ḥūt — the companion of the whale. It is one of the most famous titles in Islamic tradition — a name that reminds us of the darkest moment of his life. And yet, it is a title of honour. Because in that dark moment, Yunus said the words that every believer in distress has repeated since: La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin.

The Prophet ﷺ said: Shall I not teach you the dua of Yunus? And he taught it to his Companions. He told them that whoever says it in any moment of distress — in any whale, in any darkness, in any hopeless place — Allah will answer him. Because the dua of Yunus was not just a dua for a specific moment — it was the model for all distress.

Since that day, Muslims have said this dua in hospitals, in prisons, in wars, in famines, in grief, in loneliness, in every kind of darkness. And every time it has been said, Allah has heard it — because the dua of His prophet carries a special weight. He who was saved from the belly of the whale teaches us the prayer of salvation.

Yunus is the prophet whose darkness became the light of every believer in distress. His moment of greatest weakness became the means of every believer's greatest strength.

dialogue.arabic: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
dialogue.translation: There is no deity except You. Exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ said: The dua of Dhun-Nun, when he called out in the belly of the whale, was heard by Allah — and if a Muslim calls out with it in any distress, Allah will answer him. It is one of the most powerful duas in Islamic tradition.
lessons.takeaway: The dua of a prophet in his darkest moment becomes the light of every believer who comes after him.

lessons.title: The Repentance of a Prophet
lessons.body:
There is a striking detail in the story of Yunus that deserves its own reflection. When Yunus made his dua in the whale, he did not say: My Lord, save me. He said: I have wronged myself. He did not ask for rescue. He did not ask for forgiveness. He did not ask for anything. He simply admitted the truth.

And Allah saved him. Not because of the request — because there was no request. Not because of the words — because the words were an admission, not a plea. Allah saved him because Yunus had returned to the very foundation of faith: the recognition of who he was before his Lord.

This is the deepest lesson of tawbah. Repentance is not a transaction. It is not 'I will do X if You give me Y.' It is not a negotiation. It is a return. It is the soul turning back toward its Maker. And when the soul returns — when it genuinely, humbly, wholeheartedly acknowledges its own wrongness before Allah — then everything else follows.

Yunus did not bargain with Allah from the belly of the whale. He did not promise good deeds if Allah saved him. He simply said: I have wronged myself. And that was enough. Because when the servant says the truth about himself, Allah responds with the truth about Himself: I am the Forgiving, the Merciful.

dialogue.arabic: إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
dialogue.translation: Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.

lessons.didYouKnow: The scholars say Yunus's dua is a model of tawbah because it contains no request. It is pure admission. This is the highest form of repentance — when the servant returns to Allah not to ask for anything, but simply because he has recognised the truth.
lessons.takeaway: The truest tawbah is the one that asks for nothing — and returns simply because Allah deserves to be returned to.

lessons.title: The Second Chance
lessons.body:
When Yunus returned to Nineveh, he found a city transformed. The people who had mocked him for years were now prostrating to Allah. The idols had been broken. The temples had been abandoned. The nation that had rejected him had come to faith — and he had missed the moment of their conversion.

Yunus had wanted to be the one who converted them. He had wanted to see the fruits of his labour. He had wanted to be there when the light dawned on his people. But Allah had reserved that moment for His own timing — and it had happened while Yunus was in the belly of the whale.

This is another lesson from Yunus's story. The outcome we desire is not always given to us in the way we want it. Sometimes the harvest comes after we have left the field. Sometimes the joy of the conversion is not for us to witness. Sometimes Allah reserves the reward for the Hereafter, not for this world.

But the reward is still ours. Yunus did not see the conversion of Nineveh — but every person who believed through his message was a reward credited to him. The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever guides someone to good will have a reward like the one who did it. Yunus guided a nation — and he will be rewarded for every soul.

His patience, his obedience, his return to Nineveh after the whale — all of it was accepted. And his place among the messengers is secure. Even when he could not see the fruits, the fruits were given to him by the One who sees all.

dialogue.arabic: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَىٰ خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ
dialogue.translation: Whoever guides someone to good will have a reward like the one who did it.

lessons.didYouKnow: Yunus returned to Nineveh and continued to guide the people for the rest of his life. Some narrations say he lived long, ruling the city with justice and teaching the people the way of tawhid. His story does not end with the whale — it ends with a faithful prophet guiding a believing nation.
lessons.takeaway: The reward for guiding others is credited to you even if you never see the harvest.

lessons.title: The Legacy of Yunus
lessons.body:
Yunus's story is one of the most complete in the Quran — a prophet who fled from his mission, was swallowed by a whale, made a dua from the depths, was saved, returned to his people, and found them already guided. Every stage of the story is a lesson.

The Prophet ﷺ said: No one should say that I am better than Yunus ibn Matta. This is a strange statement — the Prophet ﷺ, the greatest of creation, saying he is not better than Yunus? The scholars explain: it was said to prevent people from using Yunus's mistakes to belittle him. The Prophet ﷺ did not want anyone to think less of Yunus because of his flight from Nineveh. Because even a prophet who runs from his mission is still a prophet of Allah.

The Prophet ﷺ also said: Do not say that I am better than Yunus. Not because the Prophet ﷺ was not the greatest — he was — but because the comparison itself is wrong. The prophets are not ranked by their mistakes. They are ranked by their obedience. And Yunus, in his darkest moment, was obedient to the very foundation of faith — he testified to the Oneness of Allah and he acknowledged his own fault.

Yunus's legacy is a legacy of hope. It is the hope that says: even the darkest place is not beyond the reach of Allah's mercy. Even the deepest ocean is not beyond His sight. Even the belly of a whale is a place where a servant can call upon his Lord and be heard. Yunus's story is the standing proof that there is no darkness that Allah cannot reach.

May Allah grant us the humility of Yunus in his darkness, the hope of Yunus in his distress, and the return of Yunus to his mission. Ameen.

dialogue.arabic: لَا يَقُولَنَّ أَحَدٌ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ مَتَّى
dialogue.translation: No one should say that I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.

lessons.didYouKnow: Yunus is called Yunus ibn Matta — 'Yunus son of Matta' — in the Quran. His father's name is preserved in revelation. He was a prophet of Nineveh, and his story is one of the most beloved in Islamic tradition.
lessons.takeaway: No darkness is beyond the reach of Allah — no despair is beyond the reach of His mercy.

lessons.title: The Guardian of Maryam
lessons.body:
Zakariyya (AS) was a prophet of the Children of Israel, a descendant of Harun, and the guardian of Maryam — the mother of Isa. He was a righteous man, a carpenter by trade, and the caretaker of the temple in Jerusalem. His life was quiet, humble, and devoted to the worship of Allah.

The Quran introduces him with tenderness: And her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner and put her in the care of Zakariyya. Maryam's mother had dedicated her child to the service of the temple — and Allah gave her to Zakariyya.

Every time Zakariyya entered the chamber where Maryam worshipped, he found something that made his heart stop: Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision. He said: O Maryam, from where is this? She said: It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account.

Maryam was a young girl, but she was not eating from the temple's stores. She was receiving provision directly from Allah — food that appeared in her chamber, in a locked room, where no human could have placed it. Her guardian, the prophet Zakariyya, was witnessing miracles in his own household.

dialogue.arabic: كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا الْمِحْرَابَ وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزْقًا ۖ قَالَ يَا مَرْيَمُ أَنَّىٰ لَكِ هَٰذَا ۖ قَالَتْ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ
dialogue.translation: Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision. He said: O Maryam, from where is this? She said: It is from Allah.

lessons.didYouKnow: Maryam's mother had promised to dedicate her child to the service of Allah before she was born. The Quran says: My Lord, I have dedicated what is in my womb to You, freed from worldly work, so accept this from me. Maryam was the only woman in the Quran with this honour.
lessons.takeaway: The greatest gift a parent can give a child is dedication to Allah.

lessons.title: The Secret Dua
lessons.body:
Zakariyya watched Maryam's miracles with wonder. He saw the provision from Allah arriving in her chamber. He saw a young girl given miracles that a grown prophet was not given. And something in his heart began to stir — a hope he had suppressed for years.

He was old. His wife was barren. He had no children. He had served the temple his whole life, and now he was approaching the end of his years without an heir — without a son to carry on his prophethood, without a descendant to continue his mission.

And so he made a dua. But not the kind of dua that most people make. He made it in secret. The Quran says: When he called to his Lord a private supplication. He said: My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened and my head has flared up with white hair, but never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, disappointed.

Look at the structure of this dua. He began by acknowledging his weakness — bones weakened, hair turned white. He did not pretend to be strong. He did not approach Allah with a sense of entitlement. He approached with the humility of an old man who knew his own limits.

And then he added: Never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, disappointed. He reminded Allah of His own generosity. Not because Allah needs reminding — but because Zakariyya needed to affirm his trust.

dialogue.arabic: إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُ نِدَاءً خَفِيًّا ۝ قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَهَنَ الْعَظْمُ مِنِّي وَاشْتَعَلَ الرَّأْسُ شَيْبًا وَلَمْ أَكُن بِدُعَائِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا
dialogue.translation: When he called to his Lord a private supplication. He said: My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened and my head has flared up with white hair, but never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, disappointed.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Arabic phrase nidāʾan khafiyyā — 'a private supplication' — is used uniquely for Zakariyya's dua. It describes a whisper, a voice so low that only Allah could hear. This is the etiquette of dua at its highest — private, sincere, and unheard by anyone but Allah.
lessons.takeaway: The most powerful dua is the one whispered so quietly that only Allah can hear.

lessons.title: The Request for an Heir
lessons.body:
Then Zakariyya made his specific request: And indeed, I fear my relatives after me, and my wife has been barren. So give me from Yourself an heir who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Yaqub. And make him, my Lord, pleasing to You.

Look carefully at the reasoning behind the request. Zakariyya was not asking for a son because he wanted to keep his wealth in the family. He was not asking for a son because he wanted prestige. He was asking for a son because he feared for the future of the faith after his death.

The phrase I fear my relatives after me refers to the fact that his relatives would not carry on his mission. His brothers, his cousins, his tribe — none of them shared his prophethood, his mission, his devotion. If he died without an heir, the guidance he had given to the people would die with him. There would be no one to continue the message.

His request for a son was a request for a spiritual heir — someone who would inherit his prophethood, his knowledge, and his mission. Not his house. Not his wealth. Not his name. His mission. This is the dua of a prophet who had devoted his whole life to the guidance of his people and wanted the guidance to continue after his death.

dialogue.arabic: وَإِنِّي خِفْتُ الْمَوَالِيَ مِن وَرَائِي وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَتِي عَاقِرًا فَهَبْ لِي مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِيًّا ۝ يَرِثُنِي وَيَرِثُ مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبَ ۖ وَاجْعَلْهُ رَبِّ رَضِيًّا
dialogue.translation: And indeed, I fear my relatives after me, and my wife has been barren. So give me from Yourself an heir who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Yaqub. And make him, my Lord, pleasing to You.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Arabic word waliyy — 'heir' — in Zakariyya's dua is the same word used for a spiritual guardian or protector. He was not asking for a biological heir in the ordinary sense — he was asking for a successor in the mission.
lessons.takeaway: The greatest inheritance is not wealth — it is the continuation of the mission.

lessons.title: The Angels' Announcement
lessons.body:
Zakariyya's dua was answered immediately. The Quran says: So We responded to him and gave him Yahya, and We cured for him his wife. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive.

The answer came while Zakariyya was standing in the prayer chamber, praying. The Quran describes the moment: Then the angels called to him as he stood praying in the chamber: Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah and honourable and chaste and a prophet from among the righteous.

The angel gave five descriptions of the son who was to be born. Yahya — his name, given by Allah. Confirming a word from Allah — he would bear witness to Isa as a prophet. Honourable — a man of dignity. Chaste — pure from sin. A prophet from among the righteous — the ultimate title.

Five honours, all announced before the child was born. And all of them given because his father had asked — and had asked with the right intention. Zakariyya did not ask for a son to comfort his old age. He asked for a son to serve the faith. And Allah gave him a son who would be one of the greatest prophets of the Children of Israel.

dialogue.arabic: فَنَادَتْهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي الْمِحْرَابِ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحْيَىٰ مُصَدِّقًا بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَسَيِّدًا وَحَصُورًا وَنَبِيًّا مِّنَ الصَّالِحِينَ
dialogue.translation: Then the angels called to him while he was standing, praying in the chamber: Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah, honourable and chaste and a prophet from among the righteous.

lessons.didYouKnow: The name Yahya — John in English — was given by Allah Himself, without any human intervening. The Quran says: O Zakariyya, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be Yahya. We have not assigned this name to anyone before him.
lessons.takeaway: The child born to a faithful parent becomes a gift to the entire Ummah.

lessons.title: The Sign
lessons.body:
Zakariyya was overwhelmed. He asked: My Lord, how will I have a boy when I have reached old age and my wife is barren? This was not doubt — it was wonder. He believed the message, but he wanted to know how the impossible would happen.

Allah gave him a sign: Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, though you are sound. Zakariyya would lose the ability to speak — not because of illness, but because Allah had taken his speech away. For three days and three nights, he would be unable to communicate with anyone by words. He could gesture, he could signal, but he could not speak.

The sign was designed to be unmistakable. A healthy old man — a prophet, in fact — losing his speech for three days was not something that could be dismissed as coincidence. It was a divine sign, given to strengthen Zakariyya's certainty in the announcement he had received.

And Zakariyya accepted the sign. He did not argue. He did not ask for a different sign. He simply obeyed. And when the sign came — when his speech left him for three days — he used that time not to panic, but to worship. The Quran says: So he came out to his people from the chamber and signaled to them to exalt Allah in the morning and the afternoon. Even in the middle of a divine sign, Zakariyya kept his heart on Allah.

dialogue.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ اجْعَل لِّي آيَةً ۚ قَالَ آيَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ النَّاسَ ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ سَوِيًّا
dialogue.translation: He said: My Lord, make for me a sign. He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, though you are sound.

lessons.didYouKnow: The sign of silence was not a punishment — it was a blessing. Some scholars say that during those three days, Zakariyya was so overwhelmed by the presence of Allah that he could not speak to people. His silence was a form of intimate communion with his Lord.
lessons.takeaway: When Allah gives you a sign, respond with worship — not with questions.

lessons.title: The Birth of Yahya
lessons.body:
Yahya was born. The Quran does not describe the birth itself — but it tells us the response of his father, and it gives us one of the most beautiful dialogues between Allah and a newborn prophet.

The Quran says: O Yahya, take the Scripture with determination. And We gave him judgement while still a boy. And affection from Us and purity, and he was fearing of Allah, and dutiful to his parents, and he was not a tyrant or rebellious. And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he will be raised alive.

Look at the language of this verse. Allah does not just describe Yahya — He sends peace upon him. Three times: on the day of his birth, on the day of his death, and on the day of his resurrection. These are the same words the Quran uses for Isa — and only Isa and Yahya receive this triple blessing.

And notice the first words: O Yahya, take the Scripture with determination. Allah was speaking directly to a newborn. Some scholars say Yahya was given understanding of the Torah while still an infant — that he could read and understand the scripture before most children can speak. He was a prophet from his earliest years.

dialogue.arabic: يَا يَحْيَىٰ خُذِ الْكِتَابَ بِقُوَّةٍ ۖ وَآتَيْنَاهُ الْحُكْمَ صَبِيًّا ۝ وَسَلَامٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيًّا
dialogue.translation: O Yahya, take the Scripture with determination. And We gave him judgement while still a boy. And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he will be raised alive.

lessons.didYouKnow: Only two prophets in the Quran receive this triple blessing of peace — Yahya and Isa. Both were born miraculously, both were given divine wisdom from childhood, and both faced martyrdom for their faith.
lessons.takeaway: Every child is a gift from Allah — but some are gifted with the very light of prophethood.

lessons.title: The Dutiful Son
lessons.body:
The Quran describes Yahya with three qualities that every parent dreams of: And affection from Us and purity, and he was fearing of Allah, and dutiful to his parents, and he was not a tyrant or rebellious.

Look at the order of the qualities. First: affection from Allah — he was loved by his Lord. Second: purity — his heart and actions were clean. Third: taqwa — awareness of Allah. Fourth: birr al-walidayn — kindness to his parents. And finally: he was not arrogant or rebellious.

Zakariyya had asked for an heir who would carry on his mission. Allah gave him more: a son who would be a prophet, and who would also be the kind of son any parent would pray for. Yahya did not just fulfil his mission — he honoured his parents. He was dutiful. He was loving. He was humble.

And then the final phrase: he was not a tyrant or rebellious. This is a striking description. The Quran is telling us that Yahya — a prophet who was given divine wisdom from infancy, who received peace from Allah three times over, who was the answer to his father's dua — was also humble. His greatness did not make him proud. His prophethood did not make him distant from his parents. He remained a son.

dialogue.arabic: وَبَرًّا بِوَالِدَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَكُن جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّا
dialogue.translation: And dutiful to his parents, and he was not a tyrant or rebellious.

lessons.didYouKnow: Yahya is one of only a few prophets in the Quran whose kindness to parents is specifically praised. The Quran says: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment. (Al-Ankabut 29:8) — Yahya embodied this from the very beginning.
lessons.takeaway: Greatness in the eyes of Allah includes kindness to your parents.

lessons.title: The Death of Zakariyya
lessons.body:
The Quran does not record the death of Zakariyya. But the classical narrations say he was martyred — killed by the very people he had spent his life trying to guide. The Children of Israel had grown corrupt, and Zakariyya had refused to compromise his message. He was killed for his refusal.

Some narrations say he was killed while fleeing from those who sought to harm him. Others say he was killed in the temple itself — the very temple he had served his whole life, the very temple where he had raised Maryam, the very temple where the angels had announced the birth of his son.

Whatever the details, the ending was the same. Zakariyya died a martyr for his faith — a prophet who had been promised a son in his old age, had seen that son grow into one of the greatest prophets of the Children of Israel, and had then been killed by the corruption he had spent his life fighting.

But the Quran honours him with words that no murderer can take away. It calls him a righteous servant. It calls him a man whose duas were answered. It calls him the guardian of Maryam — a role that no other prophet was given. His reward was not in this world. It was in the next.

The Prophet ﷺ said: The best of people are those who live long and do good deeds. Zakariyya lived long and did good deeds. His old age was not wasted — it was given to the service of Allah and the raising of a prophet.

dialogue.arabic: وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ زَكَرِيَّا ۚ إِنَّهُ كَانَ صِدِّيقًا نَّبِيًّا
dialogue.translation: And mention in the Book, Zakariyya. Indeed, he was a man of truth, a prophet.

lessons.didYouKnow: Zakariyya is one of the few prophets whose martyrdom is preserved in Islamic tradition. The narrations say he was killed for refusing to compromise on the truth — a model of a scholar who did not sell his faith for his life.
lessons.takeaway: A prophet's reward is not in how he dies — it is in how he lived.

lessons.title: The Legacy of Zakariyya
lessons.body:
Zakariyya's legacy is the legacy of a man who trusted Allah with the impossible. He was old. His wife was barren. He had no children. And yet he asked Allah for a son — because he knew that Allah could do what no human could.

His dua was answered. His son became a prophet. And his trust became a template for every believer who faces impossible odds. Zakariyya is the standing example in Islam that no request is too big for Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said: Nothing is impossible for Allah. Zakariyya lived that truth. He asked for what no one thought he could have — and he received it.

And his deeper legacy is his role as the guardian of Maryam. He was not just a prophet — he was the caretaker of the woman who would become the mother of Isa. He saw her miracles. He witnessed her provision from Allah. He was the first person in history to understand that Maryam was being prepared for something extraordinary.

Zakariyya is remembered for his prayer. He is honoured for his service. He is celebrated for his trust. And his name is preserved in the Quran as a model for every believer who dares to ask Allah for the impossible — and who trusts Him to answer.

May Allah grant us the trust of Zakariyya — and the answered prayers that follow. Ameen.

dialogue.arabic: رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِي فَرْدًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الْوَارِثِينَ
dialogue.translation: My Lord, do not leave me alone, and You are the best of inheritors.

lessons.didYouKnow: This dua — rabbi la tadharni fardan wa anta khayrul-warithin — is preserved in the Quran as one of Zakariyya's duas. It captures the humility of a prophet who knew that everything he had was given by Allah — and that without Him, he would have nothing.
lessons.takeaway: No request is too big for Allah — but every request must be made with trust and humility.

lessons.title: The Miraculous Birth
lessons.body:
Yahya (AS) was the son of Zakariyya — born to a father well past the age of fatherhood and a mother who had been barren her whole life. His very existence was a miracle, announced by angels before his birth.

The Quran says: So We responded to him and gave him Yahya, and We cured for him his wife. The mother who could not conceive was healed. The father who was old was given strength. And the child who was born was named by Allah Himself — Yahya — a name that had never been given to anyone before him.

But there is something else in Yahya's story that makes his birth extraordinary. The angels did not just announce a son — they announced a prophet. Before Yahya was born, Allah gave him five honours: Yahya (his name), confirming a word from Allah (a witness to Isa), honourable (a man of dignity), chaste (pure from sin), and a prophet from among the righteous. Five honours, given before his first breath.

And his father Zakariyya had not asked for a son to comfort his old age. He had asked for an heir to the mission — a spiritual successor who would carry on the guidance of the Children of Israel. Allah answered with a son who exceeded the request — a prophet, a man of purity, a witness to Isa.

dialogue.arabic: يَا زَكَرِيَّا إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَامٍ اسْمُهُ يَحْيَىٰ لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا
dialogue.translation: O Zakariyya, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be Yahya. We have not assigned this name to anyone before him.

lessons.didYouKnow: The name Yahya comes from the root ḥ-y-y, meaning life. Some scholars say Allah named him Yahya because he was the means by which the faith of the Children of Israel came to life again — and because he was a witness to the life-giving word of Allah, Isa ibn Maryam.
lessons.takeaway: Allah's answers to prayer are always greater than the prayer itself.

lessons.title: The Gift of Understanding
lessons.body:
Yahya was given understanding of the Torah while still a child. The Quran says: O Yahya, take the Scripture with determination. And We gave him judgement while still a boy.

The Arabic phrase al-ḥukm ṣabiyyā — 'judgement while a boy' — is unique. It means that Yahya was given the ability to understand, to judge, to reason, to interpret the scripture from a very young age. He was not just a child who memorised — he was a child who understood. He was not just a student — he was a teacher of the other children. Allah had placed a light in his heart that burned brighter than the light of any ordinary child.

The classical scholars say Yahya could read the Torah and understand its deep meanings before he was ten years old. Some narrations say he was given prophethood as a young boy — one of the youngest prophets in history. He did not have the long preparation that Musa had. He did not have the decades of revelation that Muhammad ﷺ received. He was simply given the truth directly — and he received it with determination.

The command take the Scripture with determination is a command we should all take to heart. Yahya did not receive the Torah lazily. He did not read it casually. He took it with quwwah — with strength, with power, with seriousness. He lived his scripture.

dialogue.arabic: يَا يَحْيَىٰ خُذِ الْكِتَابَ بِقُوَّةٍ ۖ وَآتَيْنَاهُ الْحُكْمَ صَبِيًّا
dialogue.translation: O Yahya, take the Scripture with determination. And We gave him judgement while still a boy.

lessons.didYouKnow: Yahya is one of only two prophets in the Quran who received divine wisdom as children — the other being Isa. Both were given understanding of the Scripture at an age when most children are still learning to read.
lessons.takeaway: The gift of understanding is given by Allah — but it must be received with determination.

lessons.title: The Marks of Prophethood
lessons.body:
The Quran describes Yahya with a series of qualities that every believer should aspire to. And they are given in a specific order — as if they are the marks of a truly righteous soul.

And affection from Us — and purity. And he was fearing of Allah. And dutiful to his parents. And he was not a tyrant or rebellious.

Look at each one carefully. Affection from Us — Yahya was loved by Allah. This was not affection Yahya earned — it was affection Allah granted. Purity — his soul was clean from sin, from corruption, from impurity. Fearing of Allah — he was aware of Allah's presence and power. Dutiful to parents — despite being a prophet, he honoured his human parents. Not tyrannical or rebellious — he was humble, gentle, obedient.

These five qualities describe a soul that was balanced between heaven and earth. Yahya was loved by Allah, pure from sin, aware of his Lord, kind to his parents, and humble in his interactions with everyone. He was not just a prophet — he was a complete human being, perfected by his Lord.

The Prophet ﷺ said: The best of you are those who are best to their families. Yahya lived this from his earliest years. He was a prophet, and he was a son.

dialogue.arabic: وَحَنَانًا مِّن لَّدُنَّا وَزَكَاةً ۖ وَكَانَ تَقِيًّا ۝ وَبَرًّا بِوَالِدَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَكُن جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّا
dialogue.translation: And affection from Us and purity, and he was fearing of Allah. And dutiful to his parents, and he was not a tyrant or rebellious.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Arabic word ḥanān — translated as 'affection' — is a rare word in the Quran. It refers to a tender, merciful love that comes from the depths of the heart. It is used only for Yahya and for Isa's birth — as a special gift of tenderness from Allah.
lessons.takeaway: The greatest souls are those who combine devotion to Allah with kindness to people.

lessons.title: The Peace That Follows
lessons.body:
There is a verse in the Quran about Yahya that few prophets received. It is a blessing Allah gave directly to him — a statement that carries the deepest comfort any human being can imagine:

Peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he will be raised alive.

Three days. Three moments. Three blessings. Allah is telling us that Yahya was safe at his birth — protected from the evil that surrounds the newly born. He would be safe at his death — protected from the despair and suffering that often precede it. And he would be safe at his resurrection — protected from the terrors of the Day of Judgement.

This is one of the highest honours given to any prophet in the Quran. Only Isa — the cousin of Yahya — receives the same three blessings in the same words. Both were born miraculously. Both were given wisdom in childhood. Both received the peace of Allah at every stage of their existence.

The Prophet ﷺ said that Yahya's peace will continue forever — that he is one of the greatest prophets of the Children of Israel, and that his name is a reminder of how Allah protects those who are faithful to Him.

dialogue.arabic: وَسَلَامٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيًّا
dialogue.translation: And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he will be raised alive.

lessons.didYouKnow: Only two prophets receive this three-fold blessing in the Quran — Yahya and Isa. The blessing covers the three most vulnerable moments of human existence: birth, death, and resurrection.
lessons.takeaway: The peace of Allah covers every stage of a believer's existence — from birth to resurrection.

lessons.title: The Preacher of Truth
lessons.body:
Yahya grew into a prophet — but a specific kind of prophet. He was not a lawgiver like Musa. He was not a king like Dawud. He was a preacher. His mission was to call the Children of Israel back to their covenant with Allah, to warn them against corruption, and to prepare the way for the coming of Isa.

He preached boldly. He was not afraid of the powerful. He was not afraid of the scholars. He was not afraid of the crowds. He stood in the temples and the marketplaces of Jerusalem and warned the people of their sins with a voice that echoed across the hills of Judea.

The classical scholars describe Yahya as a man of extreme simplicity. He wore clothes of camel hair. He ate only the simplest food. He lived in the wilderness, away from the corruption of the cities. He did not accumulate wealth. He did not seek luxury. He did not wish for status. He simply lived the message he preached — a living example of what it means to surrender to Allah.

The Prophet ﷺ said about him: Yahya was a man who was not concerned with the world. He was concerned only with the pleasure of his Lord. This is the essence of Yahya's preaching. It did not come from someone who was seeking anything from the world. It came from a man whose heart had no room for anything but Allah.

dialogue.arabic: إِنَّا أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ
dialogue.translation: Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality — the remembrance of the Home.

lessons.didYouKnow: Yahya is one of the few prophets whose preaching is specifically described as preparing the way for another prophet — he was the forerunner of Isa, sent to soften the hearts of the Children of Israel so they would be ready for the message of Isa.
lessons.takeaway: The one who preaches truth with sincerity is more powerful than the one who preaches with eloquence alone.

lessons.title: The Witness to Isa
lessons.body:
One of the five honours Allah gave Yahya at his birth was that he would be confirming a word from Allah — muṣaddiqan bi kalimatin min Allah. This refers specifically to Yahya's role as a witness to Isa ibn Maryam.

Yahya and Isa were cousins — their mothers Maryam and Elizabeth were close relatives. Yahya was born shortly before Isa. And from his earliest years, Yahya recognised something special about his younger cousin. The narrations say that when Isa was born, Yahya's father Zakariyya told him about the child, and Yahya knew immediately that this was the prophet the Torah had foretold.

Yahya did not just affirm Isa's prophethood — he prepared the way for it. He was the last prophet of the old covenant, sent to renew the faith of the Children of Israel and to prepare them for the messenger who would come after him. He was, in a sense, the bridge between the era of Musa and the era of Isa.

And when Isa began his ministry, Yahya stood with him. He did not fear that Isa would overshadow him. He did not worry that his own followers would abandon him for his younger cousin. He simply did what he was sent to do: confirm the word of Allah. The one who was born a prophet bowed to the one who was born of a virgin. Both served the same Lord.

dialogue.arabic: وَمُصَدِّقًا بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَسَيِّدًا وَحَصُورًا وَنَبِيًّا مِّنَ الصَّالِحِينَ
dialogue.translation: Confirming a word from Allah, and honourable and chaste and a prophet from among the righteous.

lessons.didYouKnow: Yahya is called muṣaddiqan bi kalimatin min Allah — 'confirming a word from Allah.' The 'word' is Isa, whose name appears in the Quran as kalimah min Allah — a word from Allah. Yahya's mission was to affirm the prophethood of Isa before the world knew it.
lessons.takeaway: The great servants of Allah do not compete — they confirm one another.

lessons.title: The Rejection of the Court
lessons.body:
Yahya's preaching brought him into direct conflict with the rulers of his time. Herod — the governor of Judea under Roman authority — had committed a sin that the Torah forbade. The details are preserved in both the Quranic tradition and the classical narrations: Herod had married the wife of his own brother while his brother was still alive.

Yahya could not remain silent. He stood before the people and declared the truth — that this marriage was unlawful, that it violated the law of Allah, and that it was a corruption that could not be tolerated. He did not care that Herod was powerful. He did not care that the courts and the priests had accepted Herod's sin. He cared only about the truth.

And Herod's wife — who had married her brother-in-law — hated Yahya for this. She demanded his death. She was jealous of his influence. She was furious at his condemnation. And she would not rest until Yahya was destroyed.

The classical scholars say the wife of Herod schemed until she convinced her husband to have Yahya executed. She wanted him beheaded — publicly — so that the people would see what happened to anyone who spoke the truth against the powerful. Yahya was killed for one reason: he refused to be silent about the truth.

dialogue.arabic: وَلَا تَقُولُوا لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ هَٰذَا حَلَالٌ وَهَٰذَا حَرَامٌ
dialogue.translation: And do not say about what your tongues assert of untruth: This is lawful and this is unlawful.

lessons.didYouKnow: The killing of Yahya is one of the earliest recorded examples of a prophet executed for speaking the truth to power. The Prophet ﷺ said that on the Day of Judgement, Yahya will stand as a witness against those who killed him — and his blood will testify against the tyrants of every generation.
lessons.takeaway: Speaking the truth against the powerful is one of the hardest forms of worship — and one of the greatest.

lessons.title: The Sacrifice of Martyrdom
lessons.body:
Yahya was killed — some narrations say he was beheaded, others say he was killed in another manner. But whatever the method, the outcome was the same: a prophet of Allah was martyred by the tyrants of his time.

The Prophet ﷺ said about Yahya: He was a prophet, and he was killed as a martyr. His head was brought to the tyrant's wife, and she rejoiced at his death. The narrations tell us that when Yahya was killed, his blood continued to bubble on the earth — a miracle that testified to his innocence and to the anger of Allah against those who killed him.

His martyrdom was not a defeat. It was a victory. Because when the tyrant thought he had silenced the prophet, the prophet's words lived on. His message continued. His example inspired. And his death became a witness against the tyrants of every generation.

The Prophet ﷺ said: The best of martyrs are the prophets — those who were killed in the path of Allah for the sake of the truth. Yahya was the ultimate example of this. He did not compromise. He did not bow to power. He did not sell his faith for his life. And for that, he was honoured by Allah with a peace that no executioner could take away.

dialogue.arabic: وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْوَاتًا ۚ بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ
dialogue.translation: And never think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.

lessons.didYouKnow: The death of Yahya is one of the most tragic events in prophetic history. He was killed by a man whose sin he had simply named. The lesson is severe: truth-telling can cost you your life, and Allah honours those who pay that price.
lessons.takeaway: The martyr's blood is more powerful than the tyrant's sword.

lessons.title: The Enduring Peace
lessons.body:
When Yahya was born, Allah said: Peace be upon him the day he was born. When Yahya was killed, that peace did not end. Because the peace of Allah is not the peace of this world — it is a peace that continues into the next world and the next.

The Quran says: And peace be upon him the day he dies and the day he will be raised alive. These are the two final stages of Yahya's existence. The day of his death was a day of peace — because he died as a martyr, in the way of Allah. The day of his resurrection will be a day of peace — because he will be raised among the prophets and the righteous.

His life was brief by the standards of the other prophets. He did not live to old age. He did not build a kingdom. He did not lead an army. He did not see the full fruits of his mission. And yet, the Quran honours him with a peace that even the greatest kings of his time did not receive.

This is the eternal lesson of Yahya's life. Allah does not measure us by the length of our days or the size of our achievements. He measures us by our faithfulness. Yahya was faithful for the short time he had — and Allah gave him a peace that will never end.

dialogue.arabic: وَسَلَامٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيًّا
dialogue.translation: And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he will be raised alive.

lessons.didYouKnow: The peace that Allah pronounced over Yahya is described by the scholars as salam 'azīm — a great peace. It is not just a greeting — it is a divine protection that follows him through every stage of existence.
lessons.takeaway: The peace of Allah is not limited by the length of your life — it is measured by the quality of your faith.

lessons.title: The Legacy of Yahya
lessons.body:
Yahya's legacy is the legacy of a pure soul. He was one of the youngest prophets. He was one of the shortest-lived. And yet, he is one of the most honoured in the Quran.

He was given a name by Allah before he was born. He was given wisdom as a child. He was given the mission of confirming Isa. He was given the peace of Allah at his birth, at his death, and at his resurrection. He was given a place among the righteous — the highest company in the universe.

The Prophet ﷺ said that Yahya is one of the four prophets whose names Allah has honoured the most in revelation. He is mentioned in every Friday prayer that Muslims recite when they send salam on the prophets. His name is spoken by every generation of believers who praise Allah for His servants.

Yahya did not live long. He did not rule a nation. He did not lead an army. He did not leave behind any wealth. He left behind only the truth he had spoken — and the life he had lived in service of Allah. And that was enough for Allah to honour him forever.

The Prophet ﷺ said: The best of people are those who live long and do good — but the most honoured are those who die in the way of Allah. Yahya lived a short life and did good. Yahya died a martyr for his faith. Both are the marks of the honoured.

May Allah make us among those He honours — with peace in life, peace in death, and peace in the resurrection. Ameen.

dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَىٰ أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ وَعَلَىٰ آلِ يَاسِينَ
dialogue.translation: And upon the family of the house and upon the family of Yasin.

lessons.didYouKnow: Yahya is called Yahya ibn Zakariyya — 'Yahya son of Zakariyya' — in the Quran. His father's prophethood and his own prophethood make the father-son pair one of only two in the Quran — the other being Imran and Maryam, and the grand pairing of Ibrahim and Ishaq.
lessons.takeaway: A short life lived faithfully is worth more than a long life lived without purpose.

lessons.title: The Dedicated Mother
lessons.body:
The story of Isa (a.s) does not begin with Isa (a.s) — it begins with his mother. And the Quran honours Maryam (a.s) with more mentions than any other woman in revelation. She is the only woman named in the Quran by name. She is the only woman whose story is told in an entire surah — Surah Maryam. And she is one of the four perfect women of Paradise, along with Khadijah, Fatimah, and Asiya.

Her story begins before her birth. Her mother — the wife of Imran — was pregnant and made a vow: My Lord, indeed I have pledged to You what is in my womb, consecrated to Your service. So accept this from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.

She had hoped for a son — a boy who would serve the temple, a boy who would dedicate his life to worship. But when she delivered, she found she had given birth to a girl. And she said: My Lord, indeed I have delivered a female. Not in complaint — in wonder, in surrender. Because the child she had been given was not the child she had expected. And the child she had been given would surpass every son she could have imagined.

Allah accepted her vow. Allah accepted Maryam. And from the very beginning, Maryam was set apart — not because she was born into a special family, but because her mother had dedicated her to Allah before she drew her first breath.

dialogue.arabic: رَبِّ إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِي بَطْنِي مُحَرَّرًا فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنِّي ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
dialogue.translation: My Lord, indeed I have pledged to You what is in my womb, consecrated to Your service. So accept this from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.

lessons.didYouKnow: Maryam is the only woman mentioned by name in the Quran — 34 times, more than most prophets. She is honoured in Surah Maryam (chapter 19) and Surah Aal-i-Imraan (chapter 3). Her name is recited in every Muslim prayer.
lessons.takeaway: The greatest gift a parent can give a child is dedication to Allah before the child is even born.

lessons.title: The Growth in the Temple
lessons.body:
Maryam (a.s) was given into the care of Zakariyya (a.s) — her uncle, the guardian of the temple in Jerusalem. And there, in the sacred precincts, she grew. But her growth was not ordinary growth. The Quran says: And her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner.

Every time Zakariyya (a.s) entered her chamber, he found her with provision. Food that appeared from nowhere. Fruit out of season. Water that no one had brought. And when he asked her where it came from, her answer was: It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account.

Maryam (a.s) did not become pious through the teaching of a scholar. She did not become righteous by reading books. She became righteous because Allah Himself was her teacher. She was raised by angels, nourished by miracles, and kept safe from every impurity. She was the first great female worshipper — the first woman who dedicated her life entirely to the worship of Allah.

And her chamber in the temple became a sanctuary. It was not a place of learning, not a place of community, not a place of teaching — it was a place of worship. Maryam (a.s) did not leave her chamber to be seen by the world. She stayed inside, praising Allah in the silence of her own heart. And that silence was heard by the heavens.

dialogue.arabic: كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا الْمِحْرَابَ وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزْقًا ۖ قَالَ يَا مَرْيَمُ أَنَّىٰ لَكِ هَٰذَا ۖ قَالَتْ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ
dialogue.translation: Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision. He said: O Maryam, from where is this? She said: It is from Allah.

lessons.didYouKnow: Maryam (a.s) is honoured in the Quran as qaʿidah and ṣāliḥah — devout and righteous. She is called al-ṣiddīqah — the truthful one — and al-sājidah — the one who prostrates. Her devotion is unlike any other woman in revelation.
lessons.takeaway: True devotion does not require an audience — Allah sees the worship of a heart even when it is done in silence.

lessons.title: The Annunciation
lessons.body:
One day, Maryam (a.s) was alone in her chamber when a visitor came. The Quran describes the moment: And mention in the Book, Maryam, when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east. And she took, in seclusion from them, a screen. Then We sent to her Our Angel, and he represented himself to her as a well-proportioned man.

She was terrified. A stranger had appeared in her chamber — a place where no one was supposed to enter. She said: Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing of Allah.

And the angel answered: I am only the messenger of your Lord to give you good tidings of a pure boy.

Read that again. Maryam (a.s) — a young woman who had never touched a man, who had dedicated her whole life to worship, who was known for her purity — was told she would have a son. Not just any son. A pure boy. A boy who would be immaculate, who would carry the word of Allah into the world.

Her response reveals her heart: My Lord, how will I have a boy when no man has touched me? She was not doubting — she was asking. She was not refusing — she was wondering. Because Maryam (a.s) knew the laws of nature. She knew that a woman without a husband does not have a child. And she wanted to understand.

dialogue.arabic: قَالَ إِنَّمَا أَنَا رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلَامًا زَكِيًّا
dialogue.translation: He said: I am only the messenger of your Lord to give you good tidings of a pure boy.

lessons.didYouKnow: The angel Jibril (Gabriel) appeared to Maryam (a.s) in human form — the same angel who would later bring revelation to Muhammad ﷺ. He is mentioned four times in the Quran and appears in the annunciation to both Maryam (a.s) and Zakariyya (a.s).
lessons.takeaway: When Allah announces something that seems impossible, He is not bound by the rules of the natural world — He is the One who made them.

lessons.title: The Word and the Spirit
lessons.body:
The angel gave Maryam (a.s) the explanation: Thus said your Lord: It is easy for Me. And We will make him a sign for the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter already decreed.

Look at the structure of that announcement. It is easy for Me. Allah is not bound by the ordinary — what is impossible for humans is simple for Him. A sign for the people. Isa (a.s) would not just be a prophet — he would be a miracle in himself. And a mercy from Us. His birth was not a punishment — it was a gift to all of humanity.

The Quran gives Isa (a.s) two titles that no other prophet received. He is called Rūḥun minhu — a spirit from Allah. And he is called Kalimatuhu — the word of Allah. Both of these titles point to the extraordinary nature of his creation. He was not created through the ordinary process of human generation. He was created by the command Kun — Be — the same command that created Adam (a.s) from clay and the universe from nothing.

The Quran says: Indeed, the example of Isa with Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him: Be — and he was. Both were created without the ordinary means. Both were direct creations of Allah. And both were sent as prophets to their people.

dialogue.arabic: إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَىٰ عِندَ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ ۖ خَلَقَهُ مِن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ كُن فَيَكُونُ
dialogue.translation: Indeed, the example of Isa with Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him: Be — and he was.

lessons.didYouKnow: Isa (a.s) is called Rūḥun minhu and Kalimatun minhu in the Quran. Both titles describe his miraculous creation — he was created by the divine command 'Be', not through the ordinary process of human generation. This is the Islamic understanding of Isa's (a.s) nature.
lessons.takeaway: Allah creates however He wills — with means or without, from dust or from a word.

lessons.title: The Birth of Isa
lessons.body:
The Quran describes the birth of Isa (a.s) with the tenderness of a mother's story. Maryam (a.s), overwhelmed by the weight of what was happening, withdrew to a distant place — a palm tree in the desert, far from her people. And there, in the pain of labour, she cried out: Oh, I wish I had died before this and was a thing long forgotten!

She was not complaining. She was not despairing. She was in the throes of childbirth — alone, afraid, and aware that she would face shame when she returned. She had no husband. She had no family with her. She had no one to help her bring a child into the world. And she was a woman whose purity was her greatest honour — and now that honour would be questioned by everyone who saw her.

And then, Allah answered. A voice called out from beneath her: Do not grieve. Your Lord has provided beneath you a stream. And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates. So eat and drink and be contented. And if you see from among humanity anyone, say: Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful abstention, so I will not speak today to any man.

Water. Dates. Silence. Three gifts from Allah in the moment of Maryam's (a.s) greatest need. The stream would nourish her. The dates would strengthen her. And the vow of silence would protect her from the accusations of her people.

dialogue.arabic: فَأَجَاءَهَا الْمَخَاضُ إِلَىٰ جِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ قَالَتْ يَا لَيْتَنِي مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَٰذَا وَكُنتُ نَسْيًا مَّنسِيًّا
dialogue.translation: And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said: Oh, I wish I had died before this and was a thing long forgotten!

lessons.didYouKnow: The Quran records Maryam's (a.s) cry of distress — I wish I had died before this — as a moment of her humanity. She was not a stoic, unfeeling saint. She was a woman in pain, and her honesty is preserved in revelation. This is the mercy of Allah — He accepts the honesty of His servants even in their weakest moments.
lessons.takeaway: The mercy of Allah does not require you to hide your pain — it only requires you to trust Him while you feel it.

lessons.title: The Speaking Infant
lessons.body:
Maryam (a.s) returned to her people carrying the infant Isa (a.s). And as she had feared, they accused her. The Quran records their words: O Maryam, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented. O sister of Harun, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste.

They did not attack her. They did not stone her. They asked her questions that cut deeper than stones — questions that accused her without accusing. Your father was not a man of evil. Your mother was not unchaste. In other words: So what have you done?

Maryam (a.s) did not answer. She had been commanded to observe silence, and she obeyed. Instead, she pointed to the baby in her arms. And the people were shocked — how could she ask them to speak to an infant? But then, Isa (a.s) spoke.

The Quran says: He said: Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet. And He has made me blessed wherever I am, and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive. And made me dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a wretched tyrant. And peace is on me the day I was born and the day I will die and the day I am raised alive.

An infant — a newborn baby, still in his mother's arms — spoke with the eloquence of a prophet. He affirmed his servanthood to Allah. He accepted his prophethood. He declared his mission. And in one sentence, he cleared his mother of every accusation that had been made against her.

dialogue.arabic: قَالَ إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ آتَانِيَ الْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلَنِي نَبِيًّا
dialogue.translation: He said: Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.

lessons.didYouKnow: The first words of Isa (a.s) in the Quran were a declaration of servitude to Allah — ʿabduLlāh. His very first act was to deny his own divinity and affirm that he was a servant. This is the Islamic understanding of Isa (a.s): a prophet, a servant of Allah, and nothing more.
lessons.takeaway: The first truth Isa (a.s) spoke was the most important — that he was a servant of Allah.

lessons.title: The Boy in the Temple
lessons.body:
Isa (a.s) grew up in the care of his mother Maryam (a.s), in the sacred land of Palestine. The Quran does not describe his childhood in detail — but it tells us enough. He was a prophet from the cradle. He was given the Scripture — the Injil — while still a young man. He grew in wisdom and in prophethood.

The classical narrations say Isa (a.s) was deeply devoted to the worship of Allah. He fasted during the day, prayed during the night, and spoke with wisdom beyond his years. He was known in the temple of Jerusalem as a boy of extraordinary insight — a child who could answer questions that even the priests struggled with.

The Quran says about him: And He will teach him writing and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel. Isa (a.s) was not taught by human teachers alone — Allah Himself was his teacher. He was given the Torah of Musa (a.s) and the Injil in their pure forms. He understood the Scriptures better than the scholars of his time, and he lived them more faithfully than the priests.

His mother Maryam (a.s) raised him alone. She had no husband to support her. She faced the whispers of the town every day. And yet, she raised the greatest prophet of her era — a prophet who would speak the truth so powerfully that the corrupt religious establishment of his time would want him dead.

dialogue.arabic: وَيُعَلِّمُهُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَالتَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنجِيلَ
dialogue.translation: And He will teach him writing and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Injil — the Gospel of Isa (a.s) — is one of the four revealed books mentioned in the Quran. It was a book of guidance given to Isa (a.s) for the Children of Israel. The version that exists today in the Bible is not the original Injil — it is a compilation written decades after Isa (a.s) by his followers.
lessons.takeaway: The single mother who raises a prophet of Allah will be honoured by Allah forever.

lessons.title: The First Miracle
lessons.body:
Isa (a.s) began his public ministry with a declaration that no other prophet had ever made. He said: Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet. And He has made me blessed wherever I am, and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive.

And then he added: And I came to you with a sign from your Lord. Indeed, I design for you from clay the shape of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by permission of Allah. And I cure the blind and the leper, and I give life to the dead — by permission of Allah. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.

Five miracles, all announced in a single verse. Creating a bird from clay. Healing the blind. Healing the leper. Raising the dead. Telling people what they ate and stored in their homes. Five signs — given not to prove Isa's (a.s) divinity, but to prove his prophethood.

Look carefully at the last phrase: by permission of Allah. Every miracle was done by permission. Not by Isa's (a.s) own power. Not by any divinity. But by the command and permission of Allah. This is the Islamic understanding of miracles — they are gifts from Allah, not proofs of divine status. Every prophet performed miracles, and every miracle was by the permission of the One who sent them.

dialogue.arabic: أَنِّي أَخْلُقُ لَكُم مِّنَ الطِّينِ كَهَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ فَأَنفُخُ فِيهِ فَيَكُونُ طَيْرًا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ
dialogue.translation: I design for you from clay the shape of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by permission of Allah.

lessons.didYouKnow: Isa's (a.s) miracles are almost identical to the miracles attributed to him in the Christian gospels — the bird from clay is mentioned in the apocryphal Infancy Gospel, and the healing of the blind and leper, and the raising of the dead, are preserved in the New Testament. The Quran confirms these miracles, but adds the essential qualifier: by permission of Allah.
lessons.takeaway: Every miracle is by the permission of Allah — no prophet performed any miracle by his own power.

lessons.title: The Call to Tawhid
lessons.body:
Isa (a.s) preached the same message every prophet had preached: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is the straight path. One God. One worship. One path. The message had not changed since Adam (a.s). It had not changed since Ibrahim (a.s). It had not changed since Musa (a.s). And it would not change with Isa (a.s) — nor with Muhammad ﷺ.

The Quran says: And when Isa brought clear proofs, he said: I have come to you with wisdom and to make clear to you some of that over which you differ. So fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.

Look at the phrase fear Allah and obey me. Isa (a.s) did not ask people to obey him because he was divine. He asked them to obey him because he was a prophet — and obedience to a prophet is obedience to the One who sent him. He did not claim authority for himself; he claimed authority as the messenger of Allah.

The Children of Israel had grown corrupt in the centuries since Musa (a.s). They had added to the law, distorted the scripture, and turned the worship of Allah into a business of the priests. Isa (a.s) came to purify the faith — to bring the people back to the simple truth of tawhid that Ibrahim (a.s) had established, that Musa (a.s) had preached, and that every prophet before him had defended.

dialogue.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ ۗ هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ
dialogue.translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is the straight path.

lessons.didYouKnow: Isa (a.s) is described in the Quran as a prophet sent specifically to the Children of Israel: And I was sent to the Children of Israel. His mission was not to the whole world — that would come with Muhammad ﷺ — but to a specific nation at a specific time.
lessons.takeaway: Every prophet's message was the same — the differences were only in the laws and the peoples they were sent to.

lessons.title: The Disciples
lessons.body:
Isa (a.s) gathered disciples — the ḥawāriyyūn — a small group of devoted followers who believed in his message and supported his mission. The Quran says: And when I inspired the disciples: Believe in Me and in My messenger. They said: We have believed, and bear witness that we are Muslims.
