The disciples were not scholars. They were not priests. They were ordinary men — fishermen, craftsmen, workers. And they were the first to accept Isa (a.s). The Quran honours them: And We supported Isa with the Holy Spirit. The disciples were given a special strength — the strength of faith in a message that the powerful were determined to destroy.

But there was one among them who wavered. The Quran does not name him — it merely says: And when the disciples said: O Isa, is your Lord able to send down upon us a table from the heaven? He said: Fear Allah, if you should be believers. Even the disciples wanted signs — a table from the sky, a public miracle. But Isa (a.s) taught them to trust.

The disciples represent every generation of believers. They were ordinary people — not scholars, not priests, not powerful men. They were the ones who believed when the religious establishment rejected. And Allah honoured them with a testimony in the Quran that will be recited until the end of time: We have believed. Bear witness that we are Muslims.

dialogue.arabic: وَإِذْ أَوْحَيْتُ إِلَى الْحَوَارِيِّينَ أَنْ آمِنُوا بِي وَبِرَسُولِي قَالُوا آمَنَّا وَاشْهَدْ بِأَنَّنَا مُسْلِمُونَ
dialogue.translation: And when I inspired the disciples: Believe in Me and in My messenger. They said: We have believed, and bear witness that we are Muslims.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Arabic word ḥawāriyyūn — disciples — comes from ḥawar, meaning whiteness or purity. They are described in the Quran as the anṣār of Isa (a.s) — his helpers in the way of Allah, just as the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ were the anṣār of Madinah.
lessons.takeaway: The first believers in any prophet are often the ordinary people — not the powerful, not the scholars, but the humble.

lessons.title: The Table from Heaven
lessons.body:
The disciples wanted more than words. They wanted proof. They said: O Isa, son of Maryam, is your Lord able to send down upon us a table from the heaven? He said: Fear Allah, if you should be believers. They said: We desire to eat from it and that our hearts be at rest, and that we know that you have been truthful to us, and that we be of its witnesses.

Notice the four reasons they gave for wanting the table. First, they wanted to eat from it — a physical experience. Second, they wanted their hearts to be at rest — certainty. Third, they wanted to know Isa (a.s) was truthful — verification. Fourth, they wanted to be witnesses — testimony. These were not idle requests. They were the requests of sincere souls who wanted to be absolutely sure.

Isa (a.s) prayed: O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table from the heaven to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You. And provide for us, and You are the best of providers.

And Allah answered: Indeed, I will send it down to you, but whoever disbelieves after it, I will punish him with a punishment which I have not inflicted on anyone among the worlds. The table came down. It was a sign for the disciples — a gift from Allah to strengthen their faith. But it was also a warning: those who saw the sign and still disbelieved would face a punishment unlike any other.

The table from heaven is a reminder that signs are not for entertainment. They are tests. Every sign that Allah sends is a mercy to those who believe and a judgment on those who refuse.

dialogue.arabic: قَالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَا أَنزِلْ عَلَيْنَا مَائِدَةً مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيدًا لِّأَوَّلِنَا وَآخِرِنَا وَآيَةً مِّنكَ
dialogue.translation: Said Isa, the son of Maryam: O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table from the heaven to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You.

lessons.didYouKnow: The story of the table from heaven is preserved in Surah Al-Ma'idah — the fifth chapter of the Quran, which is named after this table. The surah is one of the last revealed to Muhammad ﷺ and contains the final rulings of Islamic law.
lessons.takeaway: Every sign from Allah is a test — a mercy for the believer and a judgment for the rejecter.

lessons.title: The Plot Against Isa
lessons.body:
The religious establishment of Jerusalem — the priests, the scholars, the Sanhedrin — began to plot against Isa (a.s). He had exposed their corruption. He had called them out for adding to the law and distorting the scripture. He had gathered a following among the common people. And they feared him.

The Quran says: And when Isa perceived disbelief from them, he said: Who will be my helpers to Allah? The disciples said: We will be the helpers of Allah. We have believed in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims.

Look at what Isa (a.s) asked. He did not ask for defenders. He did not ask for followers. He asked for helpers to Allah. His mission was not to protect himself — it was to spread the message of tawhid. And even as the plot against him grew, he continued to call for helpers who would carry the message forward.

But the plot grew darker. The priests decided that Isa (a.s) had to die. They went to the Roman authorities — the occupying power of Palestine at the time — and accused Isa (a.s) of rebellion against Rome. They wanted him executed. And Rome — always suspicious of popular leaders — agreed to investigate.

dialogue.arabic: فَلَمَّا أَحَسَّ عِيسَىٰ مِنْهُمُ الْكُفْرَ قَالَ مَنْ أَنصَارِي إِلَى اللَّهِ ۖ قَالَ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنصَارُ اللَّهِ
dialogue.translation: And when Isa perceived disbelief from them, he said: Who will be my helpers to Allah? The disciples said: We will be the helpers of Allah.

lessons.didYouKnow: The plot against Isa (a.s) is one of the most documented events in the Quran. The Quran says: And they plotted, and Allah planned. And Allah is the best of planners. (Aal-i-Imraan 3:54) The plot against Isa (a.s) was real — but so was the plan of Allah.
lessons.takeaway: Every plot against the faithful is met by the plan of Allah — and Allah's plan always prevails.

lessons.title: The Substitution
lessons.body:
And then something extraordinary happened. Something so profound that the Quran says an entire group of people has been in confusion about it for two thousand years. Isa (a.s) did not die on the cross. He was not killed by his enemies. Allah raised him.

The Quran says: And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but it was made to appear so to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him, for certain. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.

Read that verse slowly. They did not kill him, nor did they crucify him. Not 'he was resurrected after being killed.' Not 'he was sacrificed for sins.' But: they did not kill him. Something was made to appear like the crucifixion. Someone else — most likely one of his betrayers — was crucified in his place. And Isa (a.s) was raised alive to Allah.

The Quran is emphatic: And they did not kill him, for certain. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. The scholars of Islam have debated the details for centuries, but the Quranic position is clear: Isa (a.s) did not die on the cross. He was raised — body and soul — to Allah. He is alive in the heavens. And he will return before the Day of Judgment.

dialogue.arabic: وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَٰكِن شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ ۚ وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ لَفِي شَكٍّ مِّنْهُ ۚ وَمَا لَهُم بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلَّا اتِّبَاعَ الظَّنِّ ۚ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِينًا ۝ بَل رَّفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ
dialogue.translation: And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but it was made to appear so to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him, for certain. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Islamic position on the crucifixion is one of the most distinctive in revelation. Isa (a.s) was not killed. He was raised alive to Allah — and he will return before the Day of Judgment to complete his mission and affirm the truth of Islam.
lessons.takeaway: Allah always protects His prophets — sometimes in ways that even the believers cannot foresee.

lessons.title: Raised to the Heavens
lessons.body:
Where is Isa (a.s) now? The Quran says Allah raised him to Himself. The Prophet ﷺ told us more in the narrations of the Isra and Mi'raj — his own night journey to the heavens. He said that he met Isa (a.s) on the second heaven, along with his cousin Yahya (a.s).

Isa (a.s) is alive. He is in the heavens. He is worshipping Allah, waiting for the moment appointed for his return. The Prophet ﷺ said: Isa (a.s) will descend before the Day of Judgment. He will marry, he will have children, he will live for forty years, and then he will die and be buried near me in Madinah.

The return of Isa (a.s) is one of the major signs of the Hour in Islam. When he returns, he will descend in Damascus, at the white minaret of the Umayyad Mosque. He will break the cross, kill the pig, and abolish the jizya. He will not bring a new religion — he will confirm the religion of Islam and rule by the Quran. He will lead the Muslims in prayer. He will fight the Dajjal (the Antichrist) and defeat him. And then he will die, and be buried in Madinah, next to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

Isa (a.s) is the only prophet in the Quran who is explicitly described as being alive in the heavens. He is the only prophet whose return is a sign of the Hour. His story does not end with his earthly life — it continues into the present and will continue until the end of time.

dialogue.arabic: وَإِن مِّنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ إِلَّا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ ۚ وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيدًا
dialogue.translation: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ said about the return of Isa (a.s): By Allah, the son of Maryam will surely descend as a just ruler. He will break the cross, kill the pig, and abolish the jizya. Wealth will be so abundant that no one will accept charity. (Sahih al-Bukhari)
lessons.takeaway: The story of Isa (a.s) is not over — the greatest chapter of it is still ahead.

lessons.title: The Truth About Isa
lessons.body:
The Quran is emphatic about the truth of Isa's (a.s) nature. He was not divine. He was not the son of God. He was not part of a trinity. He was a prophet — a servant of Allah — created by the command of Allah and sent to the Children of Israel.

The Quran says: O People of the Scripture, do not exceed the limits in your religion, nor say of Allah anything but the truth. The Messiah, Isa, son of Maryam, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Maryam and a soul from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And do not say: Three. Desist — it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is but one God. Exalted is He above having a son.

Read that verse slowly. The Messiah, Isa, son of Maryam, was but a messenger of Allah. The Quran honours Isa (a.s) with the title al-Masīḥ — the Messiah. It honours him as a word from Allah and a soul from Allah. It honours him as one of the greatest prophets. But it stops short of divinity. Because Isa (a.s) himself never claimed to be divine. His very first words in the Quran were: Indeed, I am the servant of Allah.

The Prophet ﷺ said: Do not praise me excessively as the Christians praised Isa (a.s). I am only a servant. So say: The servant of Allah and His messenger. The Prophet ﷺ foresaw the danger of exaggeration — of taking a beloved prophet and elevating him beyond his station. And he warned against it. He called himself what Isa (a.s) called himself: ʿabduLlāh wa rasūluh — the servant of Allah and His messenger.

dialogue.arabic: إِنَّمَا الْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُ أَلْقَاهَا إِلَىٰ مَرْيَمَ وَرُوحٌ مِّنْهُ
dialogue.translation: The Messiah, Isa, son of Maryam, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Maryam and a soul from Him.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Quran honours Isa (a.s) with titles of the highest respect — al-Masīḥ (the Messiah), Kalimatuhu (His word), Rūḥun minhu (a soul from Him). But it explicitly forbids the claim that he was divine or the son of Allah. Isa (a.s) himself denied this in the Quran.
lessons.takeaway: The truest way to honour a prophet is to describe him the way Allah described him — and nothing more.

lessons.title: The Question on the Day of Judgment
lessons.body:
The Quran closes the story of Isa (a.s) with a scene from the Day of Judgment. A scene that brings tears to the eyes of every believer who reads it. Allah will ask Isa (a.s) directly: O Isa, son of Maryam, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?

And Isa (a.s) will answer with words of overwhelming humility: Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, it is You who is Knower of the unseen. I said not to them except what You commanded me: Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Observer over them, and You are, over all things, Witness. If You should punish them — indeed they are Your servants; but if You forgive them — indeed it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

Read that answer slowly. Isa (a.s) does not defend himself with excuses. He does not point fingers at his followers. He does not claim any right. He simply says: I only said what You commanded. And now the matter is Yours. His humility on the Day of Judgment will be perfect. The prophet who was worshipped by millions will stand before his Lord and say: I only ever called them to worship You.

And Allah will respond with a declaration that ends the entire discussion of Isa's (a.s) nature: This is the Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness. For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, Allah being pleased with them, and they with Him.

dialogue.arabic: مَا قُلْتُ لَهُمْ إِلَّا مَا أَمَرْتَنِي بِهِ أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمْ
dialogue.translation: I said not to them except what You commanded me: Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.

lessons.didYouKnow: This scene from Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:116-118) is one of the most important passages in the Quran about Isa (a.s). It preserves his final testimony about his own mission — that he called only to tawhid, and that he never claimed divinity.
lessons.takeaway: On the Day of Judgment, the only defence a prophet needs is that he said only what Allah commanded.

lessons.title: The Legacy of Isa
lessons.body:
Isa (a.s) is one of the greatest prophets of Allah — one of the five messengers of strong will (ulū al-ʿazm) along with Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and Muhammad ﷺ. He is the Messiah. He is the Word of Allah. He is a Spirit from Allah. He was born of a virgin, spoke as an infant, and performed miracles by the permission of Allah. He was raised alive to the heavens. He will return before the Day of Judgment. And he will die, and be buried in Madinah, next to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

His legacy is a legacy of pure tawhid. He called the Children of Israel back to the worship of the One God — the same message every prophet had carried. He healed the sick, raised the dead, and gave sight to the blind — all by the permission of Allah. He was gentle, humble, and utterly devoted to his Lord.

The Quran honours him with a verse that appears in every Muslim prayer: Peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive. Every Muslim who recites the tashahhud in prayer sends salam upon Isa (a.s) — because the Prophet ﷺ taught us to bless the family of Ibrahim (a.s), which includes Isa (a.s).

The greatest lesson of Isa (a.s) is his humility. He was a prophet whose birth was a miracle, whose life was a miracle, and whose future is a miracle. And yet his first words were: Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. And his last words to his people were: I only said what You commanded — worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. He never claimed to be more than a servant. And because he was a perfect servant, Allah honoured him above all other prophets except Muhammad ﷺ.

May Allah grant us the humility of Isa (a.s), the purity of Maryam (a.s), and the devotion of the disciples. Ameen.

dialogue.arabic: وَسَلَامٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيًّا
dialogue.translation: And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he will be raised alive.

lessons.didYouKnow: Isa (a.s) is mentioned 25 times in the Quran — more than any other prophet except Musa (a.s). He is called by 12 different names and titles in revelation. His story spans multiple surahs including Al-Imran, Maryam, Al-Ma'idah, and An-Nisa.
lessons.takeaway: The greatest servants are those who never claim greatness — and Allah raises them the highest.

lessons.title: The Orphan of Makkah
lessons.body:
Muhammad ﷺ was born in Makkah in the year 570 CE — in a city of idols, in a tribe that had forgotten the way of Ibrahim (a.s). His father, Abdullah, had died before he was born. His mother, Aminah, passed away when he was six years old. He was raised by his grandfather Abdul-Muttalib for two years, and then — when his grandfather also passed — by his uncle Abu Talib.

An orphan in a tribal society. A boy with no father to defend him, no mother to comfort him, no wealth to command respect. And yet, from his earliest years, the people of Makkah saw something extraordinary in him. They called him al-Ṣādiq — the truthful. And they called him al-Amīn — the trustworthy. Before he received any revelation, before he was a prophet, before anyone knew who he would become, his character had already made him the most respected young man in his city.

The Prophet ﷺ later said: I was sent to perfect good character. And this was no accident — his entire life before prophethood was a training in character. He learned patience as an orphan. He learned gratitude as a poor man. He learned leadership as a trusted shepherd. Allah prepared him through every trial before He called him to the greatest mission in human history.

dialogue.arabic: وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ
dialogue.translation: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ never received any formal education. He could neither read nor write. He grew up as an orphan, in a city of idolaters, in a remote corner of the world. And yet he delivered the most eloquent revelation in human history — because his teacher was Allah Himself.
lessons.takeaway: The trials of your childhood are not wasted — they are the training for your mission.

lessons.title: The First Revelation
lessons.body:
At the age of forty, Muhammad ﷺ began retreating to the cave of Hira, on a mountain outside Makkah, to reflect on the corruption he saw around him. He had never worshipped idols. He had never participated in the shirk of his people. His heart was searching for the truth — the truth of Ibrahim (a.s), the truth of the one God his people had abandoned.

And then, one night in Ramadan, the Angel Jibril (Gabriel) came to him. The Prophet ﷺ described the moment: He came to me while I was in the cave, and he said: 'Iqra — Read!' I said: 'I do not know how to read.' He seized me and squeezed me until I could bear it no longer. Then he released me and said: 'Iqra — Read!' I said: 'I do not know how to read.' He seized me again and squeezed me a second time until I could bear it no longer. Then he released me and said: 'Iqra — Read!' I said: 'I do not know how to read.' He seized me a third time, then released me and said: Read in the name of your Lord who created — created man from a clinging substance. Read, and your Lord is the most Generous — who taught by the pen — taught man that which he knew not.

The first word of the Quran was Iqra — Read. The first command of the final revelation was not to pray, not to fast, not to fight. It was to read. To learn. To know. The religion of Islam begins with a call to knowledge, and the first revelation was the beginning of a book that would change the world.

dialogue.arabic: اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ ۝ خَلَقَ الْإِنسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ ۝ اقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ ۝ الَّذِي عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ
dialogue.translation: Read in the name of your Lord who created — created man from a clinging substance. Read, and your Lord is the most Generous — who taught by the pen.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ was 40 years old when the first revelation came. He was in the cave of Hira on the mountain of light, near Makkah, in the month of Ramadan. The night is commemorated as Laylat al-Qadr — the Night of Power — which is celebrated every Ramadan.
lessons.takeaway: The first word of the Quran was 'Read' — because the road to knowing Allah begins with seeking knowledge.

lessons.title: The Three Years of Silence
lessons.body:
The first revelation was followed by a period of silence. Some narrations say it lasted a few months; others say longer. During this time, the Prophet ﷺ waited. He had heard the voice of Jibril. He had received the first verses. And then — nothing. No new revelation. No new instructions. Just the silence of the cave and the weight of what he had experienced.

Some scholars say this silence was a mercy. The Prophet ﷺ needed time to process what had happened. He needed time to prepare for the enormous mission ahead. He needed time to understand that the revelation was not a single event — it was the beginning of a lifelong relationship with Allah.

And then, when the silence was at its heaviest, the revelation returned — and with it, a new command. The Prophet ﷺ was told: O you who covers himself, arise and warn. And your Lord glorify. And your clothing purify. And uncleanliness avoid.

Look at the order. First: arise. He had been lying down, covered in a blanket, exhausted from the weight of the revelation. He was told to stand. Then: warn. His mission was to warn his people. Then: glorify your Lord. Then: purify your clothing. Then: avoid uncleanliness. Every command built on the one before. First the self, then the community, then the Lord. First purification, then proclamation.

This is the beginning of the public mission. The Prophet ﷺ stood up from the cave of Hira, walked into Makkah, and began to call his people to tawhid.

dialogue.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُدَّثِّرُ ۝ قُمْ فَأَنذِرْ ۝ وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ ۝ وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ
dialogue.translation: O you who covers himself — arise and warn. And your Lord glorify. And your clothing purify.

lessons.didYouKnow: The surah that resumed revelation — Surah Al-Muddathir — is one of the shortest in the Quran. But it contains the entire blueprint of the Islamic mission: stand up, warn the people, glorify Allah, purify yourself, and avoid corruption.
lessons.takeaway: Every mission begins with the purification of the self — you cannot call others to Allah if you are not first standing before Him.

lessons.title: The Years of Persecution
lessons.body:
The Prophet ﷺ began his public mission by calling the people of Makkah to tawhid. At first, the response was cautious. But slowly, the message spread — and with it, the anger of the powerful. The Quraysh leaders realised that if the message of Muhammad ﷺ succeeded, their temples, their idols, and their entire economy would collapse.

So began thirteen years of persecution. Bilal (r.a) was dragged through the streets with a rope around his neck. Sumayyah (r.a) became the first martyr of Islam — she was killed for refusing to curse the Prophet ﷺ. Yasir (r.a) was tortured to death. The early Muslims were beaten, starved, imprisoned, and mocked. Some were boycotted by their own families. Others were driven out of their homes.

And through all of it, the Prophet ﷺ did not retaliate. He did not call for violence. He did not curse his enemies. He did not ask Allah to punish the people of Makkah. He simply continued to call them to tawhid — with patience, with mercy, and with a heart that never wavered.

The Prophet ﷺ was offered wealth if he would stop preaching. He was offered kingship. He was offered women. He refused all of it. He said: By Allah, if they placed the sun in my right hand and the moon in my left to make me abandon this mission, I would not — until Allah makes it victorious or I perish in its cause. This is the heart of a prophet — a heart that cannot be bought, bribed, or broken.

dialogue.arabic: وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ يَضِيقُ صَدْرُكَ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ
dialogue.translation: And We already know that your heart is strained by what they say.

lessons.didYouKnow: The first martyr of Islam was Sumayyah bint Khayyat (r.a), the mother of Ammar ibn Yasir (r.a). She was killed by Abu Jahl for refusing to renounce her faith — the first blood spilled in the way of Allah for this Ummah.
lessons.takeaway: The price of truth is often persecution — but the reward of truth is a place in the highest ranks of Paradise.

lessons.title: The Year of Sorrow
lessons.body:
In the tenth year of the mission, the Prophet ﷺ faced two losses that shook the very foundations of his life. His wife Khadijah (r.a) — his companion of twenty-five years, the first believer, the woman who had supported him through everything — passed away. And his uncle Abu Talib — the man who had protected him from the Quraysh for over a decade, the only reason he had survived the early years — also died.

The Prophet ﷺ called that year ʿĀm al-Ḥuzn — the Year of Sorrow. Two of the pillars of his life had fallen. His wife, who had comforted him when the entire world opposed him. His uncle, who had stood as a wall between him and the swords of the Quraysh. And now both were gone.

With Khadijah gone, the Prophet ﷺ lost his closest companion. The house that had been a place of peace became a place of memories. With Abu Talib gone, the Prophet ﷺ lost his protection. The Quraysh now had no reason to restrain themselves. The persecution grew worse. The stones grew larger. The threats grew louder.

And still, the Prophet ﷺ did not waver. He did not complain. He did not give up. He simply continued — carrying the weight of his losses, holding onto his faith, and trusting that Allah would not abandon him.

This is one of the most important lessons of the Prophet's life. Even the greatest of creation faced the deepest of sorrows. Even the Prophet ﷺ wept. Even the Prophet ﷺ grieved. And yet he never stopped turning to Allah. His grief did not become despair. His losses did not become excuses.

dialogue.arabic: فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا ۝ إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
dialogue.translation: For indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease.

lessons.didYouKnow: Khadijah (r.a) was the Prophet's ﷺ first wife and the first Muslim. She supported him with her wealth, her patience, and her love for 25 years. The Prophet ﷺ said: She believed in me when the people disbelieved. She was the mother of my children and the love of my heart.
lessons.takeaway: The grief you carry is not a sign that Allah has abandoned you — it is a sign that He is preparing you for something greater.

lessons.title: The Night Journey
lessons.body:
In the midst of the Year of Sorrow, Allah gave the Prophet ﷺ a gift that no other prophet had received. He was taken from Makkah to Jerusalem, and from Jerusalem to the seven heavens, in a single night. This is the Isrā' wal-Miʿrāj — the Night Journey and the Ascension.

The Quran says: Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.

The Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Burāq — a heavenly steed — from Makkah to Jerusalem. There, at the Al-Aqsa Mosque, he met all the prophets of Allah — Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and every other prophet from the beginning of time. He led them in prayer. He was affirmed as the imam of the prophets, the final messenger, the seal of the line.

Then, from Jerusalem, he ascended through the seven heavens. In each heaven, he met a prophet — Adam (a.s) in the first, Isa (a.s) and Yahya (a.s) in the second, Yusuf (a.s) in the third, Idris (a.s) in the fourth, Harun (a.s) in the fifth, Musa (a.s) in the sixth, and Ibrahim (a.s) in the seventh. In each heaven, the prophets welcomed him. In each heaven, the ranks of the angels greeted him.

And then he was brought to the presence of his Lord. He was given three gifts: the five daily prayers, the final verses of Surah Al-Baqarah, and the promise that anyone who dies without associating partners with Allah will be forgiven. The Prophet ﷺ returned to Makkah that same night — but he returned with gifts that would carry the Ummah for the rest of time.

dialogue.arabic: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا مِّنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى
dialogue.translation: Exalted is He who took His Servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa.

lessons.didYouKnow: The five daily prayers were not brought down by an angel — they were given directly to the Prophet ﷺ by Allah in the heavens on the Night of Mi'raj. This is why they are called ʿibādah rūḥiyyah — the spiritual worship. Every Muslim who prays five times a day is honouring a gift given directly to the Prophet ﷺ.
lessons.takeaway: The prayers you pray today were gifted to the Prophet ﷺ in the heavens — they are a treasure that only you can open.

lessons.title: The Hijrah
lessons.body:
After thirteen years of persecution in Makkah, Allah gave the Prophet ﷺ permission to migrate. The Muslims left their homes, their tribes, their wealth, and their memories — and travelled to Madinah, a city that had accepted Islam and welcomed the Prophet ﷺ as its leader.

The migration is called the Hijrah. It marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar. It marks the beginning of the Muslim community — the Ummah — as a political and social entity. And it marks the beginning of a new chapter in the history of Islam.

The Prophet ﷺ himself left Makkah in secret, with Abu Bakr (r.a) as his only companion. They hid in a cave — the cave of Thawr — while the Quraysh searched for them. The Quran describes the moment: When they were in the cave, and he said to his companion: Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us.

Look at the Prophet's ﷺ certainty. He had been driven from his city, hunted by his people, with a price on his head. And yet, sitting in a cave, with the enemy footsteps above them, he told Abu Bakr: Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us. He did not say 'I hope Allah is with us.' He did not say 'perhaps Allah will help us.' He said: Allah is with us. Certainty. Unshakeable. Absolute.

The Hijrah was not a defeat — it was a strategy. The Prophet ﷺ did not leave Makkah because he was weak. He left because the mission needed a land where the message could grow. And Allah had prepared Madinah to receive him.

dialogue.arabic: إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا
dialogue.translation: When he said to his companion: Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Islamic calendar begins with the Hijrah — not with the birth of the Prophet ﷺ, not with the first revelation, but with the migration to Madinah. This shows how important the establishment of the Muslim community is in Islam.
lessons.takeaway: Sometimes the greatest victories come from walking away from what you cannot change — and building something new.

lessons.title: The Constitution of Madinah
lessons.body:
When the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah, he did not just become the leader of the Muslims. He became the leader of an entire city — including Jews, pagans, and Muslims from different tribes. And he did something that had never been done before in Arabia: he wrote a constitution.

The Ṣaḥīfah — the document known as the Constitution of Madinah — laid out the rights and responsibilities of every citizen of the city. It guaranteed religious freedom for the Jews. It protected the rights of the pagans. It created a system of mutual defence. It established that every citizen — regardless of their religion — had the right to a fair trial. And it created the first truly pluralistic society in the history of Arabia.

This is one of the most important political documents in human history. It shows that Islam is not a religion that forces belief — it is a religion that guarantees the freedom of conscience. The Prophet ﷺ did not force the Jews of Madinah to accept Islam. He did not force the pagans to convert. He allowed them to worship as they wished. Because the Quran says: There is no compulsion in religion.

And this is what the Muslims built in Madinah: a city where justice was for everyone. Where the weak were protected. Where the stranger was welcomed. Where the orphan was fed. Where the slave could become a leader. Where the man who had been driven from his home in Makkah could become the greatest leader Arabia had ever seen.

dialogue.arabic: لَا إِكْرَاهَ فِي الدِّينِ ۖ قَد تَّبَيَّنَ الرُّشْدُ مِنَ الْغَيِّ
dialogue.translation: There is no compulsion in religion. The right course has become clear from the wrong.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Constitution of Madinah is one of the earliest known written constitutions in human history. It guaranteed rights to Jews, pagans, and Muslims alike — long before the concept of religious freedom became a modern political principle.
lessons.takeaway: Islam is not a religion of force — it is a religion of invitation and free choice.

lessons.title: The Conquest of Makkah
lessons.body:
After eight years in Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ returned to Makkah — not as a fugitive, but as a conqueror. He entered the city with an army of ten thousand Muslims. He entered without bloodshed, without vengeance, without retribution. He entered with his head bowed low on his camel — a gesture of humility before Allah, not pride before men.

The people of Makkah had tortured his companions. They had killed his family. They had driven him from his home. They had spent twenty years fighting against him. And now, they were at his mercy. They stood outside the Kaaba — the very house they had filled with idols — waiting for the Prophet's ﷺ judgement.

And the Prophet ﷺ asked them one question: O Quraysh, what do you think I am going to do with you?

They answered: We hope for good. You are a noble brother, the son of a noble brother.

And the Prophet ﷺ said the words that would echo through every generation of Muslims: I say to you what Yusuf said to his brothers: No blame will be upon you today. Go — you are free.

No punishment. No bloodshed. No vengeance. Twenty years of persecution answered with total forgiveness. The Prophet ﷺ did not just conquer Makkah — he conquered the hearts of its people. And within days, the entire city had accepted Islam.

dialogue.arabic: اذْهَبُوا فَأَنْتُمُ الطُّلَقَاءُ
dialogue.translation: Go, for you are free.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah with his head bowed so low that his beard nearly touched his camel's saddle. He was not entering as a proud conqueror — he was entering as a humble servant of Allah, grateful for the victory his Lord had granted him.
lessons.takeaway: The greatest victory is not the one that defeats your enemy — it is the one that makes them your friend.

lessons.title: The Farewell Sermon
lessons.body:
In the final year of his life, the Prophet ﷺ performed the Hajj — his only Hajj after the Hijrah. Over one hundred thousand Muslims gathered at Mount Arafah to hear him speak one final time. And what he said was not about himself — it was about us. It was about the Ummah. It was about the legacy he was leaving behind.

He said:

O people, listen to my words, for I do not know whether I will meet you again after this year.

Your lives and your property are sacred — like the sacredness of this day, in this month, in this city.

Allah has forbidden you to take usury. So all interest obligations shall henceforth be waived.

Beware of Shaytan, for he has lost all hope of misleading you in great matters — but he is content to mislead you in small matters.

Worship Allah, establish your five daily prayers, fast in Ramadan, give the zakat, and perform the Hajj. Listen to your leaders — even if they are slaves from Abyssinia.

All mankind is from Adam and Eve. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor a non-Arab over an Arab. A white person has no superiority over a black person, nor a black person over a white person — except by piety and good action.

I am leaving behind two things: the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet. If you hold onto them, you will never go astray.

O people, your Lord is one. Your father is one. You are all the children of Adam — and Adam was from dust.

And then he said: Have I delivered my message?

And the hundred thousand Companions replied: Yes.

And the Prophet ﷺ raised his finger to the sky and said: O Allah, bear witness.

Three months later, the Prophet ﷺ passed away. He was sixty-three years old. He had spent twenty-three years as a prophet. He had transformed a city of idolaters into the centre of tawhid. He had built the greatest community in human history. He had been given the Quran — the final, guarded, perfect word of Allah. And he had left behind a legacy that would be carried by Muslims until the end of time.

His final words, as he lay dying, were: O Allah, with the highest companionship.

And he was buried in Madinah, in the room of Aishah (r.a), where his masjid still stands. Over one billion Muslims around the world face Makkah when they pray — but every Muslim who visits Madinah can say salam to him directly. He is still there. Waiting. Sleeping in peace.

And one day, we will hear his voice in the next world — as the greatest intercessor for the Ummah.

Peace be upon him, and upon all the prophets of Allah. Ameen.

dialogue.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ وَاحِدٌ، وَإِنَّ أَبَاكُمْ وَاحِدٌ، كُلُّكُمْ لِآدَمَ وَآدَمُ مِنْ تُرَابٍ
dialogue.translation: O people, your Lord is one and your father is one. All of you are from Adam, and Adam was from dust.

lessons.didYouKnow: The Prophet ﷺ said: I am the final prophet. There is no prophet after me. And he said: My Ummah is the best Ummah — you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. The Prophet ﷺ was the seal of the prophets — the final messenger of Allah to all of humanity.
lessons.takeaway: The Prophet ﷺ did not leave us alone — he left us the Quran and the Sunnah, and promised we would never go astray if we held onto them.
